newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish '96 CPI seen between 17.9-18.2 pct - fin min.
newsitem.headline: Polish '96 CPI seen between 17.9-18.2 pct - fin min.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said on Friday consumer price inflation should fall to between 17.9 percent and 18.2 percent at the end of the year.
"The question is now whether inflation will be at 17.9 percent at best or 18.2 percent under the worst scenario," Kolodko told a news conference.
Year-on-year inflation was 19.5 percent in September and 21.6 percent at the end of 1995.
Kolodko said the final outcome of his battle against inflation would depend on how the market behaves during the pre-Christmas shopping season.
"We face a question of how the market will react during the pre-holiday season," Kolodko said.
Earlier on Friday, Kolodko said the October month-on-month inflation was 1.36 percent.
The government set this year's inflation target at 17 percent but later revised its forecast to 17.8 percent in its 1997 budget draft.
